learning: Check first whether the single line-loss event happens at start-up (progress near 0) or on a bend (progress above 0.1). If it is at start-up, the entry speed and sensor reach are the cause. If it is on a bend, steering gain is the cause.
notes: Integrates the Builder's narrow 12 mm row at y = 0.04 with a rescaled controller: kp reduced to keep steering gain near baseline, kd raised to damp faster signal changes, base_speed lowered to reduce start-up drift. The race will be the first test of this controller on the narrow row.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the wide five-sensor row (x = -0.04 to 0.04, y = 0.06) with kp 2.0, kd 0.2 and base_speed 1.6. All 60 trials went off track with no finishes. Progress reached only 0.11 to 0.15, and each run had exactly one line-loss event. Max error reached about 0.06 m, the off-track limit for this body. Steering oscillation was highest on the slalom (0.153) and s-bend (0.143). The Builder's iteration 1 geometry narrows the row to x = -0.02 to 0.02 at 10 mm spacing and moves it to y = 0.04. I have accepted that geometry unchanged, because it is the variable under test. The controller is rescaled for it. The narrow row has half the lateral span, so the same weights would double the steering slope per metre. I set weights to -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1 on the narrow row, which keeps the slope at about 50 per metre. I then reduced kp from 2.0 to 1.2, which gives an effective gain of about 60 per metre, close to the baseline's 50 per metre. I raised kd from 0.2 to 0.3 to damp the faster signal changes that a narrow row produces. I lowered base_speed from 1.6 to 1.3 because the robot is leaving the line before it stalls, and slower entry should reduce drift at start-up and on the first sharp bend. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup. line_loss stays last_direction so this iteration isolates the geometry change. Expected result: fewer off-track endings and lower steering oscillation on the slalom and s-bend. Completion is not expected from this iteration alone. I have not measured any of this.
